contract.note: Checked all 19 documented fields on the real SC-489 row (container-level id/project_id/project_ids/report_type/title/description/report_timeframe/report_creation_mode/custom_date_range/frequency/frequency_details/next_run_at/is_scheduled/created_at/owner/mail_to/report_filters/dynamic_filters/latest_attachment) in both directions — every declared field was present with the declared type, and no extra field appeared. Specifics: `id` really is the SC-NNN string form ("SC-489"), not an integer — no drift like batch 2's custom-field id. `report_type` ("Test Run Summary") and `report_creation_mode` ("custom_report") both fall inside their declared closed enums. `frequency` returned "once" for this unscheduled report, matching the contract's documented substitution rule for a null stored frequency. `is_scheduled: false` is consistent with `frequency_details: null`. `owner` is exactly `{email, full_name}` with no user id exposed, as documented. `mail_to` has the documented `{users: [], external_mails: []}` shape; both arrays are empty, consistent with the contract's note that mail_to is 'populated only for scheduled reports' (this one is not). `dynamic_filters: null` is confirmed true for this record, consistent with the contract's 'always null on this surface' claim — though this is a sample of one, so 'always' remains asserted only for this row, not proven universally. `report_filters: {}` matches the declared object type; this particular report was created with last_one_week/no explicit filters so the sub-claim that it 'echoes back public identifiers' could not be exercised (nothing was configured to echo) — the field's type conforms but that specific behavior is untested by this sample. `latest_attachment: null` and `custom_date_range: null` are both consistent with a freshly-created, non-custom-timeframe, ungenerated report. Container-level `scheduled_report_count` (0) and `total_report_count` (1) are exactly right given one unscheduled report exists — and confirms the clean 0→1 transition against the baseline this same probe established before create_report ran.

notes: Baseline (established by this capability's own first pass, before the sibling create_report probe ran): project PR-2005 (__mcp-capability-fixture__) had 0 reports (total_report_count=0, scheduled_report_count=0, reports=[], no SC-NNN ids). After create_report created SC-489, re-probing this same capability shows total_report_count=1, scheduled_report_count=0 (SC-489 is_scheduled=false) — exactly the expected 0→1 transition, confirming the sibling's write and this capability's read agree. Row-shape verification is based on a single real record (SC-489); it checks out cleanly (PASS) on every declared field in both directions, but several sub-claims that only apply to non-default states — mail_to actually populated for a scheduled report, report_filters echoing real TR-NNN/TP-NNN identifiers, next_run_at/frequency_details holding real schedule data, latest_attachment populated, custom_date_range populated — were not exercised because this sample happens to be an unscheduled report with default/empty values in exactly those fields. Verdict PASS reflects what was checked, not a claim that every documented edge case was exercised. Re-probing initially hit preprod's outage twice in a row ('the product could not be reached', status 0) before succeeding on the third attempt with identical arguments — consistent with the standing caution that this error is an environment issue, not a capability defect; no argument changes were needed between attempts 2, 3 and the successful probe. No writes were made by this capability or by this re-probe; SC-489 was read only, never modified or deleted, per instructions treating it as shared read-only fixture data with the sibling probe.
